subject: research/mimic-mauve
professional: a senior NLP researcher who evaluates generative text models with MAUVE and divergence-frontier metrics (Pillutla et al. 2021; JMLR 2023 follow-up); first checks: is MAUVE computed correctly from the quantised histograms, does results.json reproduce from the code, is the human-vs-human null a fair comparison (same feature space, same n), are sample sizes and bucket counts in a regime where MAUVE is stable, are cross-cell statistics valid given shared human pools, and is the nearest prior work on embedding choice for MAUVE cited

evidence.correctness: Ran it. In a scratch copy (scratchpad/research/mimic-mauve, mimic-contexts symlinked) with a fresh venv (numpy 2.5.5, scipy 1.18.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1, mauve-text 0.4.0, faiss-cpu 1.16.0), `python mauvecheck.py` rewrote results.json and results.txt byte-identical to the committed files (cmp exit 0), and figure.py rewrote experiments/figure.svg byte-identical. Independent recomputation (scratchpad/audit/indep.py, my own divergence frontier from the paper's definition: R_l = lP+(1-l)Q, point (exp(-c KL(Q||R)), exp(-c KL(P||R))), c = 5, area closed with (0,1),(1,0)) applied to the library's own p_hist/q_hist in every one of the 200 MAUVE calls of a full replay: max |indep - library| = 2.2e-16; with a 20,001-point grid instead of the library's 25 points the area moves by at most 6.8e-4, below the third decimal the README reports. Closed forms: identical histograms give 1.000000; disjoint supports give 0.0039683 against the analytic 5*B(5,6) = 1/252 = 0.0039683. AUROC replaced by my own Mann-Whitney U and distinct-2 by my own bigram counter reproduce every cell to 2.2e-16 and 0. Spearman recomputed with my own tie-aware ranks: -0.6015 (t = -3.19, df 18, p ~ 0.005) and 0.2406 (t = 1.05, p ~ 0.31), matching results.json. The computation is right; what limits the score is not arithmetic but the interpretation (claims, domain).
evidence.completeness: README claims checked end to end: the 4 unittest tests run (OK, 0.8 s); mauvecheck.py produces results.json/results.txt for 20 cells with n 48 to 100 as stated; figure.py produces the SVG; the human-vs-human null, the 2-fold cross-fit char 1-4 gram AUROC and distinct-2 are all computed as described in Method; data path ../mimic-contexts/data/suite.jsonl.gz exists. No stubs or TODOs. Gaps: no requirements file pins the versions that give byte-identical output; README runtime 'about 2 minutes' could not be checked cleanly (15 min wall here with 3 other jobs on 2 CPUs).
evidence.verification: `venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v` -> Ran 4 tests, OK. Four seeded mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py plus one equivalent: distinct-2 bigram offset w[1:] -> w[2:] caught; detector score sign flipped caught; null drawn from the same humans as h1 (h[n:2n] -> h[:n], so null = 1 by construction) SURVIVED; dropping the len(human)//2 cap on n SURVIVED (would make h2 short or empty on small families); label flip [0]*n+[1]*n -> [1]*n+[0]*n survived but is an equivalent mutant (the classifier is trained on the same flipped labels). Nothing tests main(), the summary statistics, or that the null halves are disjoint; the core claim (null vs test separation) has no test that would catch a broken null.
evidence.craft: Read mauvecheck.py (130 lines), figure.py, tests/test_mauvecheck.py. Small, readable, deterministic (RandomState(0) stream shared across cells; byte-identical rerun). Defects: no requirements/lock file although output depends on sklearn/faiss/mauve-text versions; results written next to the script with no output-dir option (an auditor must copy the tree); per-draw MAUVE and null values are discarded (only mean and sd kept), so the separation claim cannot be checked from results.json; files opened without context managers. No dead code or copied engines.
evidence.claims: Checked against results.json: null range 0.924 to 0.985 mean 0.964 (README 0.92 to 0.99, 0.964) pass; max test MAUVE 0.830 wiki/mistral-chat pass; Spearman -0.60 p 0.005 and 0.24 p 0.31 pass; recipes llama/mistral AUROC 0.999 MAUVE 0.32, news/llama 0.97/0.75 pass; distinct-2 mpt-chat poetry 0.839 vs 0.829, reddit 0.804 vs 0.747, MAUVE 0.12/0.25 pass; sd 0.004 to 0.21 pass; n 48 to 100 pass. Fails: README.md:15 'Every cell is far from its null ... separates machine text from human text in all 20 cells' compares cell means only; from the per-draw replay (scratchpad/audit/out/draws.json) wiki/mistral-chat draws 2 and 3 give test 0.918/0.901 against their own nulls 0.919/0.902 (indistinguishable), and recipes/mpt-chat draw 5 gives 0.978, above 4 of its 5 null draws. No per-cell test is run. The same sentence is repeated in research/README.md:779. 'and the reverse' (README.md:17) has no cell backing it (every low-MAUVE cell has AUROC >= 0.99). Limitations, 'Preliminary, stylised' framing and AI-assistance note are present and honest about GPT-2 features.
evidence.fitness: A researcher could rerun the pipeline and swap in GPT-2 features later, which is the stated next step. Nearest prior work is not cited: Pillutla et al. (JMLR 2023, 'MAUVE scores for generative models: theory and practice') already studies MAUVE under different embeddings and sample sizes and compares it with classifier-based measures, and Pimentel et al. (ICLR 2023, 'On the usefulness of embeddings, clusters and strings for text generator evaluation') shows MAUVE with clustered embeddings largely tracks surface/lexical features. Against those, 'lexical-embedding MAUVE loosely agrees with a lexical n-gram detector' is expected rather than new, and the interesting disagreements (news, recipes) are within the per-cell noise and embedding sensitivity below. Not part of any programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md.
evidence.domain: Departures from MAUVE practice: (1) sample size: the paper's text experiments use thousands of samples per side; here n = 48 to 100 with num_buckets = n/10 = 5 to 10 k-means clusters (faiss warns 'please provide at least 195 training points'), a regime where MAUVE is high-variance and biased, acknowledged only as 'noisy'. (2) Feature space differs between test and null: the SVD is refit on h1+g for the test and on h1+h2 for the null (mauvecheck.py:69-70), unlike a fixed feature extractor. My check with one embedding fit on h1+h2+g (scratchpad/audit/sharedemb.py, fresh draws): wiki/mistral test mean 0.850 vs null 0.978 (separation holds), but news/llama test mean 0.536 vs the script's 0.749 (sd 0.16, different draws), so cell values move by amounts comparable to the cross-cell differences the 'disagree where it is interesting' bullet reads. (3) The Spearman p-value treats 20 cells as independent though cells in a family share one human pool (7 families), so p = 0.005 is optimistic. Five draws, reported sd and an explicit null are good practice.

No test checks the null halves are disjoint or the n cap: seeding null = h1 vs h1 (MAUVE 1) or dropping len(human)//2 leaves all tests green

verdict: The computation is right and reproducible: results.json, results.txt and the figure rebuild byte-identically, and my own divergence-frontier implementation on the library's histograms, closed-form cases (1 and 1/252), Mann-Whitney AUROC, bigram counter and rank correlation all match to machine precision. It falls short of a MAUVE practitioner's sign-off on interpretation: the headline 'every cell far from its null' fails per draw in 2 of 20 cells, MAUVE is run at n = 48 to 100 (5 to 10 buckets) where it is noisy and embedding-sensitive, the Spearman p ignores shared human pools, the nearest prior work on embedding choice is uncited, and the tests would not notice a broken null. Finished (completeness 3), does not meet the bar (claims 2, verification 2, median 2).
